prompt:
A neighbor has returned a borrowed tool late twice, but is otherwise friendly. Suggest a courteous boundary for future borrowing. A response of around 120 words is enough.

Write the requested response as one self-contained paragraph of plain text. Do not use a title, headings, bullet points, numbered lists, Markdown formatting, code fences, or line breaks. Include only the requested content, without any introductory or closing commentary from the assistant. Keep the approximate word target given in the task. If the task calls for an email, dialogue, steps, or calculations, express that content within the same paragraph.
base_prompt: A neighbor has returned a borrowed tool late twice, but is otherwise friendly. Suggest a courteous boundary for future borrowing. A response of around 120 words is enough.
text: Keep the boundary friendly, specific, and focused on getting your tools back when you need them: “I’m happy to help when I can, but the last couple of times, the tool came back later than we agreed. Going forward, I’ll need us to agree on a return day and time before I lend anything out. If that timing won’t work, no worries, but I’ll need to keep it here.” Choose deadlines that genuinely suit you, and feel free to decline when you can’t risk a delay. If another agreed deadline is missed, you can calmly say, “I’m going to take a break from lending tools, but I appreciate your understanding.” You can stay neighborly without continuing an arrangement that doesn’t work for you.
